regions: Coastal southern state of temples, hills and the Krishna-Godavari deltas.
Himalayan frontier of misty valleys, monasteries and tribal cultures.
Tea gardens, the Brahmaputra, one-horned rhinos and warm hospitality.
Land of Bodh Gaya's enlightenment and ancient Pataliputra.
Waterfall-dotted central state of tribal heritage and dense forests.
Sun-drenched beaches, Portuguese heritage and laid-back river life.
Wide salt deserts, wild lions, craft villages and the western coast.
North Indian heartland of history, wetlands and farmlands.
Pine-clad Himalayan hill country of trekking trails and rivers.
Forest plateau of falls, hills and tribal arts.
Palace cities, ancient ruins of Hampi, coffee hills and beaches.
Backwaters, spice plantations, hill stations and tropical coast.
The heart of India — forests, forts, temples and wildlife.
Cosmopolitan coast, Sahyadri ghats, caves and hill retreats.
Lush valley state of the Loktak lake and classical dance.
Abode of clouds — wettest places, living root bridges, pine hills.
Blue-green ridges and rivers of the eastern frontier.
Warrior tribal state of the Hornbill festival and rugged peaks.
Temple city fields, sacred Konark sun wheel and quiet coasts.
Golden Temple city, fertile fields and a hearty food culture.
The royal desert state of forts, palaces, dunes and vibrant fairs.
Himalayan kingdom of monasteries, peaks and rhododendron forests.
Dravidian temples, hill stations and the Coromandel coast.
Biryanis, lake-side gardens and Qutb Shahi heritage.
Northeastern state of royal palaces and lush hills.
The Taj Mahal, ghats of Varanasi and the vast Gangetic plains.
Land of gods, Himalayan char dham and alpine adventure.
Himalayan Darjeeling, mangrove Sundarbans and cultural Kolkata.
Crystal islands of turquoise water, coral reefs and rainforest.
Le Corbusier's planned garden city on the Punjab-Haryana border.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu
Sunny western coast towns and riverside interiors.
Seven cities of empire — Red Fort, Qutub, markets and modern India.
Snow peaks, lakes, tulip gardens and Himalayan meadows.
High-altitude moonscapes, monasteries and world-class high passes.
A coral atoll archipelago of startlingly clear lagoons.
French colonial quarter, Auroville and a calm Coromandel coast.

destinations.name: Gulmarg
destinations.summary: India's premier ski bowl set in alpine conifer meadows at 2,690 m.
destinations.description: A bowl of rolling alpine meadows ringed by the Apharwat ridge. Reachable by road from Srinagar (52 km); the Gulmarg Gondola, one of the highest cable cars in the world, lifts skiers to 3,979 m in two phases.
local: Phase II Gondola ride to Kangdori
Golf at one of the world's highest courses
seasons: Powder season; check gondola phase-II weather conditions.
Melting snow, crisp air, flowers returning.
Best for avoiding crowds at a lower price.
Peak family season; snow gone above treeline except Apharwat.
activities: Slopes served by gondola phase I and II with rentals and instructors on-site.
Dramatic ride from Kongdori to 3,979 m above the valley.
One of the highest golf courses in the world set in meadow surroundings.
Frosted pines and blue-hour light over the Apharwat range.

destinations.name: Srinagar
destinations.summary: Houseboats, Dal Lake shikaras and Mughal gardens in the Kashmir Valley.
destinations.description: The summer capital of Jammu & Kashmir, served by Srinagar airport (12 km) with direct flights from major metros. The walled old city, Mughal gardens and Dal Lake define a city as romantic as it is historic.
local: Sunrise shikara ride on Dal Lake
seasons: Chinar trees blaze gold in crisp air.
activities: Glide past floating vegetable gardens and lotus beds as the sun rises over Zabarwan hills.
Terraced gardens of Nishat, Shalimar and Chashma Shahi.
Overnight aboard a walnut-carved houseboat with local cuisine.
A ceremonial Kashmiri multi-course feast in the old city.

destinations.name: Pahalgam
destinations.summary: River-side meadows at the head of the Lidder Valley — base for the Amarnath Yatra.
destinations.description: Green meadows flanking the Lidder river, 95 km from Srinagar airport. Acts as the base camp for the Amarnath cave pilgrimage each summer and a peaceful base for horse treks to Baisaran and Aru.
seasons: Crisp golden light over the river.
Many dhabas close; check road conditions.
activities: The 'mini Switzerland' meadow above Pahalgam with panoramic valley views.
Film-set green valley accessible by shared cabs.
Licensed river fishing on the Lidder.
Access point for the cave shrine (July-August, registration required).

destinations.name: Leh
destinations.summary: High-desert capital of Ladakh under the Stok Kangri range.
destinations.description: Ladakh's gateway at 3,500 m, reached by Kushok Bakula Rimpochee airport or the Manali/ Srinagar highways. Expect Buddhist monasteries, the Leh Palace and dramatic driving passes on every side.
seasons: Below -20C at night; roads mostly closed.
Only for the prepared; connectivity cut.
activities: Monastery backdropped by the Indus valley peaks with early light.
Drive onto one of the world's highest motorable passes.
June mask-dance festival at Ladakh's largest monastery.
Quirky roadside optical illusion and a mountain-war memorial.

destinations.name: Nubra Valley
destinations.summary: A hidden gem of sand dunes, cold desert bactrian camels and twin continental rivers.
destinations.description: Reached over the Khardung La, Nubra's Indus-Shyok confluence creates a cold desert of dunes and apricot orchards. Permits required; stay in Hunder or Diskit.
local: Bactrian camel ride on Hunder dunes
seasons: Cool and sunny with warm dunes.
Khardung La closed; valley snowed in.
activities: Two-humped camels on the Hunder sand dunes, a cold-desert oddity.
Hilltop monastery housing the giant Maitreya statue overlooking the valley.
Sulphur springs tucked at the head of Nubra.

destinations.name: Manali
destinations.summary: The classic Kullu Valley adventure town at the foot of Rohtang Pass.
destinations.description: A lively two-kilometre riverside town in the Kullu Valley, 48 km from Kullu-Bhuntar airport and connected by deluxe Volvos from Delhi. Base for Solang valley adventure sports and the Rohtang/Atal tunnel road to Lahaul.
seasons: Snow down to town level; -5C to 8C.
activities: Paragliding, zorbing, quad biking and an aerial ropeway 14 km from Manali.
Snow-slope skiing and lessons during the winter months.
Rapids between Pirdi and Jhiri as the snow melts.
Rooftop cafes over the Beas run by backpacker culture since the 70s.

destinations.name: Shimla
destinations.summary: The colonial summer capital on a pine ridge above the Sutlej valley.
destinations.description: Reachable by the Kalka-Shimla heritage toy train or road from Chandigarh (113 km). Mall Road, the Ridge, Victorian cottages and snow views define this former summer capital of British India.
seasons: Snow showers and clear ridge views.
Daffodils and cherry blossoms in the parks.
activities: UNESCO-listed narrow-gauge ride through 102 tunnels and snowfall pines.
Pedestrian spine of colonial Shimla with Himalaya views.
Highest point in town with a giant Hanuman statue and monkey residents.
One of Asia's largest natural outdoor rinks, open in deep winter.

destinations.name: Dharamshala
destinations.summary: Tibetan exile capital and misty Kangra valley hill town.
destinations.description: Home of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, with an hour's drive from Kangra airport under the Dhauladhar peaks. McLeod Ganj, the Namgyal monastery, trekking and a rich tea culture anchor the town.
activities: Attend debate and prayer sessions of the Dalai Lama's main temple.
A 9 km climb from Dharamkot to a ridge camp with glacier views.
Main temple, museum and Kalachakra circles in one courtyard.
Kangra tea estates and Tibetan handicraft ateliers.

destinations.name: Spiti Valley
destinations.summary: A cold-desert Himalayan valley of ancient monasteries, ranked among India's great offbeat drives.
destinations.description: The middle Himalayas' cold desert, reached from Kaza along the high Kinnaur-Spiti road (opens May/June). Key, Kibber and Tabo monasteries stud the Spiti river canyon. Permits and hardy winter gear required.
seasons: Blue skies, warm days, cold nights.
Roads and homestays open from June.
Arid gold light and crystal night skies.
activities: Cliff-perched medieval monastery with murals and 300 monks.
Moon lake at 4,300 m on the Kunzum side, a starlit desert pool.
One of the world's highest inhabited villages and ancient fossil sites nearby.
Some of India's darkest skies for astro shots.

destinations.name: Jaipur
destinations.summary: The Pink City of forts, bazaars and royal courtyards — gateway to Rajasthan.
destinations.description: Rajasthan's capital behind cobride walls, served by Jaipur international airport and rail to Delhi (300 km). Amber Fort, Hawa Mahal and the City Palace form a heritage triangle of the first rank.
activities: Hilltop rajput palace reached by shared jeeps or elephants.
The winds' palace facade and Johari Bazar's gem and textile lanes.
Sunset terrace over the Pink City walls.
Lake palace and old-city water architecture.

destinations.name: Udaipur
destinations.summary: The 'city of lakes' framed by the Aravali hills — Rajput romance on water.
destinations.description: Built around Lake Pichola under the Aravali ridge, 250 km from Jaipur with a small airport and rail connection. City Palace, lake palaces and ghat life make it the most photographed city in Rajasthan.
seasons: Warm and blooming round the lakes.
Rain refills Fateh Sagar and Pichola.
activities: Golden-hour ride past Jag Mandir to the island palace.
A layered mahal of courtyards, peacock mosaics and lake views.
The Great Wall of India — a 36 km fort perimeter 82 km away.
Dance show and museum on the lake's edge.

destinations.name: Jaisalmer
destinations.summary: The golden fort city rising from the Thar desert.
destinations.description: A walled sandstone town 575 km west of Jaipur, within a night train from Delhi and reachable by the Jodhpur-Jaisalmer line. Fort, havelis and Sam Dunes camel safaris define the desert experience.
seasons: The only season for easy camping.
Thar's rare rain greens the dunes.
activities: Sunset camel trek and star-camp on the western dunes.
A 12th-century fort still inhabited and honeycombed with temples.
A five-brother merchant mansion carved in gold sandstone.
Tank-side monasteries and temples at dusk.

destinations.name: Jodhpur
destinations.summary: The blue city beneath the Mehrangarh citadel.
destinations.description: Rajasthan's second city, 300 km from Jaipur on the main Delhi rail corridor. The ridgetop Mehrangarh Fort and a labyrinthine blue old city are the anchors.
activities: Among India's great citadels with palace galleries and a chauki durbar.
Brahmin quarter lanes painted in indigo wash above the clock tower.
Ornate 18th-century water architecture now ringed by cafes.
Restored arid landscape under the fort with native flora trails.

destinations.name: Pushkar
destinations.summary: A holy lake town of ghats, camels and the world's largest camel fair.
destinations.description: A compact sacred town 145 km from Jaipur around the Pushkar lake. Its annual November camel fair and the only Brahma temple in India pull pilgrims and travellers alike.
seasons: Cool fair season with the camel fest in Kartik.
Book months ahead for the fair.
activities: November's giant camera-friendly livestock and bazaar fair.
Rare shrine to Brahma with the 52 temple ghats below.
Hilltop climb for a golden view over the lake.
Sunset lamps set afloat on the sarovar.

destinations.name: Agra
destinations.summary: Home of the Taj Mahal — the moon-white mausoleum of love.
destinations.description: Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri and the Taj sit on the Yamuna, 200 km from Delhi by train or the new Yamuna Expressway. Sunrise entry to the Taj is the signature ritual.
activities: Entry at dawn for pink-marble light before the crowds.
1500-ft red-sandstone fortress with palace views to the Taj.
Akbar's abandoned imperial ghost city, 40 km west.
Watch pieta dura artisans practicing Taj-era craft.

destinations.name: Varanasi
destinations.summary: The eternal city on the Ganga — ghats, aartis and winding lanes.
destinations.description: One of the world's oldest living cities, on the Ganges with direct rail from Delhi and an airport 22 km out. Dawn boat rides and the Dev Deepawali aarti are the core experiences.
activities: Subah-e-Banaras glide past the ghats as the city wakes.
Large evening fire-and-lamp ceremony on the main ghat.
The newly opened Golden Temple approach.
Buddha's first-sermon site with the Ashoka pillar, 10 km away.

destinations.name: Mathura-Vrindavan
destinations.summary: Birthplace of Krishna — temple-dense sacred towns on the Yamuna.
destinations.description: Twin holy towns 150 km from Delhi on the Agra road (with dedicated rail). Temples, Govardhan hill and a raw devotional tempo define the experience, peaking at Holi and Janmashtami.
activities: Illuminated marble temple with evening light-and-kirtan show.
Sacred baths and tiny shrines down to the river.
The world-famous stick-festival village, a March ritual.
Krishna's childhood pastures and parikrama hill.

destinations.name: Rishikesh
destinations.summary: Yoga capital of the world on the Ganges — ashrams, rafting and beach cafes.
destinations.description: An ashram-lined town where the Ganges leaves the mountains, 25 km from Dehradun airport and 240 km from Delhi. Yoga teacher trainings, Laxman Jhula and Grade-3 white-water rafting anchor the scene.
seasons: Winter sun is on the river.
activities: Marine Drive stretch rapids from Shivpuri, grades 2-3 with guides.
Morning ashtanga and pranayama at ghat-side studios.
Trek to the ashram cave then the waterfall above the river.
Sunset lamp ceremony under the Lakshman Jhula at dusk.

destinations.name: Mussoorie
destinations.summary: Queen of the hills — a mist-loved colonial ridge town.
destinations.description: A deodar-and-coffee hill station 35 km from Dehradun airport, with the Mall Road ridge walking spine and the Himalayan range behind Kempty falls. Weekend favourite of Delhi.
seasons: Rains and mists lock the ridge.
activities: Flat ridge promenade with the full Himalayan horizon.
Short tram to the ridge's highest point.
Cascading terraces 15 km out, famous for picnics.
Terraced gardens and an orchard sunset point.

destinations.name: Nainital
destinations.summary: The emerald lake town cradled by seven hills.
destinations.description: A pear-shaped Naini lake ring of a hill town, 300 km from Delhi and 64 km from Kathgodam railhead. Boating, the high-altitude Naini peak and the zoo-mall circuit define it.
activities: Rowing boats and early light on the tear-drop lake.
A Himalayan shrine at the lake's northern corner.
Horse ride to a picnic knoll above the northern ridge.
Winter sledging slope at the far end of the lake.

destinations.name: Auli
destinations.summary: A garhwali ski slope and ropeway above the Nanda Devi amphitheatre.
destinations.description: An open snow bowl at 2,519-3,050 m with a cable-car link from Joshimath and a road from Badrinath highway. India's most popular beginner ski slopes with a famous 12-km deodar trek.
activities: Beginner-to-intermediate runs with certified instructors and rentals.
Asia's longest public cable car with layered ridge views.
A 3 km trail to a lookout over the Nanda Devi range.
Forest temple climb and a mirroring lake.

destinations.name: Darjeeling
destinations.summary: The queen of Himalayan hill stations — tea gardens and the toy train.
destinations.description: A tea-country ridge town 88 km from Bagdogra airport, famous for the Kanchenjunga sunrise at Tiger Hill and the UNESCO Darjeeling Himalayan Railway. Tea estates and Ghoom monastery complete the mix.
activities: A steam joy-ride on the UNESCO-listed toy train.
A working 19th-century estate fractioned out to pluckers and pressers.
Spiral rail loop and the high-altitude monastery viewpoint.

destinations.name: Sundarbans
destinations.summary: The world's largest tidal mangrove forest — the tiger's estuary kingdom.
destinations.description: A UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of delta islands between Kolkata and Bangladesh, entered from Sonakhali/Godkhali (100 km from Kolkata). Boat safaris seek the Royal Bengal tiger, estuarine crocs and Gangetic dolphins.
seasons: Dry, cool, animal movements on bank.
activities: Multi-hour motorized prowl through mangrove channels.
Sudhanyakhali and Sajnekhali towers with tiger-print mudbanks.
Herons, kingfishers and muddy island waders.
Gangetic dolphins in the estuary channels at dawn.

destinations.name: Gangtok
destinations.summary: Sikkim's hill capital of monasteries, cable cars and Kanchenjunga framing.
destinations.description: A neat hill city 124 km from Bagdogra airport and a short drive from the Tsomgo lake road. Rumtek monastery, the ropeway and weekend views of Kanchenjunga make it Sikkim's basecamp.
seasons: Cold and clear with snow roads above.
activities: The largest monastery in Sikkim, seat of the Karmapa.
Pedestrian heart of Gangtok and a cable swoop over the valleys.
Sacred glacial lake at 3,780 m on the Nathu La road (permits).
Tibetan stupa complex and the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

destinations.name: Kaziranga
destinations.summary: One-horned rhino country — a UNESCO grassland river park.
destinations.description: A 430 sq km national park on the Brahmaputra floodplains, 192 km from Guwahati airport on the NH27. Elephant-back and jeep safaris in its tall elephant-grass meadows are the draws.
seasons: Dry grass opens; rhino most visible.
Hot but animals at water points.
activities: Rhino, wild buffalo, hog deer and hornbills from open-top vehicles.
Dawn rides closest to grazing rhino.
Falls and ruined temples just outside the park.
Darters, herons and the Bengal florican in marginal wetlands.

destinations.name: Majuli
destinations.summary: The world's largest river island, shaped by the Brahmaputra's braids.
destinations.description: An erosion-threatened island world of neo-Vaishnavite sattras (monasteries), mask makers and weaving, reached by ferry from Jorhat (nearest airport/rail). A serene, genuinely offbeat stopover.
activities: Watch paper-bamboo mask artisans rehearse Raas drama.
15 km of paddy lanes linking sattras and weaving cooperatives.
The return crossing in orange evening light.
Overnight meals and weaving in stilt-house villages.

destinations.name: Shillong
destinations.summary: The Scotland of the East — pine hills above the Assam plains.
destinations.description: Meghalaya's capital, 103 km from Guwahati airport but a rain-softened green landscape of its own. Ward's Lake, the Crinoline falls viewpoints and nearby Mawphlang sacred groves make it a gentle base.
activities: A wooden walkway and rowboats around a tree-lined lake.
Three-tier cascade in the pine forest below town.
A 1,000-year protected forest with monoliths, 25 km out.
Night market for garlic chutney, khasi crafts and street food.

destinations.name: Cherrapunji
destinations.summary: Sohra — the world's wet capital of living root bridges and cascades.
destinations.description: 1,489 m above the plains and once the wettest place on Earth. The double-decker living root bridge at Nongriat and the valley-edge outlooks reward a short, steep descent from Sohra town.
seasons: Falls at full ferocity, mud settles.
Root bridge descent dangerous in rain.
activities: A 3,500-step descent to Nongriat's two-level living bridge.
India's tallest plunge waterfall falling into a churning plunge pool.
A lit limestone cave of stagmites and bats.
A cliff panorama of Bangladesh plains and the plains below.

destinations.name: Tawang
destinations.summary: A high-altitude Buddhist enclave crowned by India's largest monastery.
destinations.description: A 300-km winding road from Tezpur/Guwahati towards the Bhutan-China borderlands brings you to Tawang at 3,048 m. The 17th-century monastery, Sela Pass and the Madhuri lake define a genuinely far-flung journey.
activities: Founded 1680-81, the largest monastery in India with a golden Buddha hall.
4,170 m pass with a glassy high-altitude lake.
Pristine sky-blue lakes off the monastery road.
A glimpse of the sacred Gorichen (6,858 m) from Tawang.

destinations.name: Puri
destinations.summary: Seaside home of the Jagannath Temple and the sacred Blue Flag beach.
destinations.description: One of the four dhams, on the Odisha coast 60 km from Bhubaneswar airport and rail. The Rath Yatra, the state's finest beach and the neighbouring Konark Sun Temple make a complete Odisha circuit.
activities: The 12th-century shrine and dining hall behind the sacred precinct.
Blue Flag beach with rolling morning surf.
A 13th-century chariot-temple of the sun, a World Heritage jewel.
Asia's largest brackish lagoon with Irrawaddy dolphins.

destinations.name: Khajuraho
destinations.summary: The Chandela temple ensemble — India's greatest sculptural gallery.
destinations.description: A UNESCO group of Nagara-style temples built 950-1050 CE, served obliquely by Chhatarpur rail and Khajuraho airport (limited flights). The Western Group's dance figures and the sound-and-light show are unmissable.
seasons: Clear cool days for temple touring.
Feb dance festival is the highlight.
activities: The sculptural perfection of Kandariya Mahadeo under dawn or dusk light.
Narration of temple lore projected over the western group at night.
Classical Bharatanatyam and Kathak against the temple backdrop.
A granite-canyon gorge 18 km out with stepping-stone cascades.

destinations.name: Pachmarhi
destinations.summary: The satpura plateau's emerald canopy — MP's only hill station.
destinations.description: Dense forest, honeycomb caves and sandstone stacks set a thousand metres up, 210 km from Jabalpur rail. Bee Falls, Jatashankar caves and the sunset point of Dhoopgarh make it a quiet 2-3 day retreat.
activities: The highest point of the Satpuras with layered ridge views.
A chute of water into a ferns-laced pool.
A mythology-steeped cave beneath overhanging rock.
Rock-cut shelters and a two-sided gorge viewpoint.

destinations.name: Bhimbetka
destinations.summary: A cave gallery of some of humanity's oldest rock paintings.
destinations.description: Over 700 rock shelters with paintings that span 100,000 years of human art, 45 km from Bhopal air/rail. A half-day site visit with the famous 'boar hunt' panel — a quiet, extraordinary hidden gem.
seasons: Cool and clear for shelter walks.
Open sunrise to sunset minus Mondays.
activities: Drinker-bull and boar-hunt panels across the Buffer Zone shelters.
The largest shelter, named for its acoustically rich bell chamber.
See excavated tools and the ancestry of the paintings in Bhopal.

destinations.name: Ahmedabad
destinations.summary: Gandhi's Sabarmati city — a World Heritage walled heart.
destinations.description: The first UNESCO-listed Indian city, on the Sabarmati with a modern metro and full air/rail connectivity. Pol houses, the Sabarmati Ashram and street food anchor the experience.
activities: Latitude of carved wooden havelis and bird feeders in the walled quarter.
Gandhi's 1917 riverside base and the Dandi march's starting point.
Jewellers by day; hive of egg and jalebi stalls by night.
Intricate ornate well five storeys deep, 20 km north.

destinations.name: Rann of Kutch
destinations.summary: The white salt desert — India's photogenic winter moonland.
destinations.description: A seasonal salt marsh of the Great Rann, 90 km from Bhuj airport via Dholavira/Mandvi roads. The Rann Utsav (Nov-Feb) brings tents, crafts and full-moon rituals to the white desert.
activities: Salt pan magenta light and mirror photography at dusk.
The Rann's only hill with a 360-degree white horizon.
Embroidery, bell-making and leatherwork hamlets of the Banni belt.
A species of albino camel trotting the dry salt crust.

destinations.name: Gir National Park
destinations.summary: The last wild home of the Asiatic lion.
destinations.description: A teak flat-forest park 60 km from Junagadh and 350 km from Rajkot airport. Lion safaris are booked online through Sasan Gir; jeeps comb the dry teak for the park's 600+ lions and a full cat graveyard of prey.
seasons: Cool clear visibility in open teak.
Book lion-safari jeeps on the official portal.
Heat is brutal; use closed-jacket safari.
activities: Gir's raison d'etre — licensed jeep or canter with trackers.
Observation point teeming with muggers near the HQ village.
Photographic pastures of open water in the regulated sanctuary.
Mountain temple climb and Jain derivation views near Junagadh.

destinations.name: Mumbai
destinations.summary: The city that never sleeps — gothic arches, sea-drives and street food.
destinations.description: India's financial and film capital on the Arabian Sea, with its own dense airport web and full rail. Gateway of India, Marine Drive, the CSMT gothic quarter and king-prawn fry define it.
activities: Basalt triumphal arch built 1924, hub of harbour life.
A ferry to 5th-7th-century Shiva rock-cut caves.
The queen's necklace neon sweep along the bay.
Legendary late-night kebab and biryani lanes.

destinations.name: Lonavala
destinations.summary: The Sahyadri's weekend monsoon chai-stop — forts, lakes and caves.
destinations.description: A plateau-side station between Mumbai and Pune with a tiny airstrip hub via Pune (65 km). Karla-Ellora caves, Lion's Point and monsoon slips of the Western Ghats at 620 m keep it eternally popular.
activities: Gushing stair-runs of the monsoon wall.
Ancient Brahmanical caves with granite prayer-hall frontage.
Scalloped viewpoints over the Western Ghats escarpment.
A bluff-shaped ledge climb above the old Mumbai-Pune road.

destinations.name: Goa
destinations.summary: India's beach classic — 100 km of coast, churches and cashew sunsets.
destinations.description: A land of coconut palms and Portuguese churches between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, reached through its own international airport, Madgaon rail and the Konkan route. Beach shacks, night markets and easy living define it.
activities: Red-cliff views and flea markets behind the beach.
Basilica of Bom Jesus and whitewashed cathedral complexes.
A four-tier cascade reachable by train crossing over the gorge.
Banana rides, parasailing and jet-ski on the state's busiest beach.

destinations.name: Mysuru
destinations.summary: The sandalwood city of palaces and puja-lit streets.
destinations.description: Two hours from Bengaluru airport/rail on the NH275, Mysuru's Amber-lit palace, Devaraja market and the Chamundi hill view make a courtly classic. The Dussehra festival is its crown.
activities: The Amba Vilas interiors lit on Sundays and during Dasara.
Thousands of steps and a giant Nandi above the city.
Garlands, turmeric heaps and spice mountains in the heart of town.
Water-dance fountain show at Krishnaraja Sagar dam, 20 km out.

destinations.name: Hampi
destinations.summary: The stone-boulder capital of the Vijayanagara empire.
destinations.description: A World Heritage landscape of granite boulders and temple masonry on the Tungabhadra, 350 km from Bengaluru and 12 km from Hospet rail. Virupaksha temple, the boulder hills and Coracle rides define it.
activities: The stone chariot and the 56-pillar musical hall.
The city's working temple enclosing daily puja at its gate.
Scramble for the full boulder-field and temple panorama.
Round woven-bamboo ferries to the far bank.

destinations.name: Coorg
destinations.summary: Madikeri — Karnataka's coffee country of misty estates and waterfalls.
destinations.description: A coffee-and-pepper Western Ghats hill country 250 km from Bengaluru, entered via Madikeri town. Abbey falls, Raja's seat and plantation stays in the emerald canopy make it a classic monsoon-lovers' retreat.
activities: Arabica fields, pepper creepers and a shade canopy tour.
A colonnaded viewpoint over the river valley.
The Kaveri's origin shrine and the triveni confluence.

destinations.name: Gokarna
destinations.summary: A pilgrim town of holy coves and India's strongest breezes.
destinations.description: A temple town on the Karnataka coast 150 km from Mangalore/air-rail. Om, Kudle and Half Moon beaches behind the monkey-hills make a rough-roads classic of the hippie route north.
activities: A double-cove in the shape of the sacred syllable.
Trail over the headland to Kudle, Half Moon & Paradise.
Atma-linga shrine where pilgrims break the beach day.
Drum circles and cliff obelisk sunsets by the coves.

destinations.name: Munnar
destinations.summary: The Western Ghats' tea-country basin of rolling emerald slopes.
destinations.description: Kerala's most famous hill station at 1,700 m, 108 km from Kochi airport. Tea museum, Eravikulam and top-station viewpoints make the loop while the monsoons bring the mists that folk songs celebrate.
activities: Withering, rolling and CTC machinery in a working estate.
The nilgiri tahr's sanctuary and Rajamala shola walks.
Boating and the dam loop amid pine plantations.
The Western Ghats staircase at the Tamil Nadu border.

destinations.name: Kochi
destinations.summary: Fort Kochi — a spice-soaked colonial port of Chinese nets and Dutch lanes.
destinations.description: Kerala's Arabian-Sea gateway with a bustling international airport and rail port. The Jewish quarter, dutch warehouses, Chinese fishing nets and Kathakali evenings stitch centuries of trade into one walkable quarter.
activities: Teak-and-stone mechanism still hauling on the Fort Kochi shore.
The Paradesi synagogue's blue Cantonese tiles and whitewashed lanes.
Full make-up demonstration and classical performance in Fort Kochi.
The working harbour crossing and ghat-side heat.

destinations.name: Alleppey
destinations.summary: The Venice of the East — Kerala's backwater heart.
destinations.description: A canal-crossed town 53 km south of Kochi airport which summons the palm-shadowed backwater runs. A houseboat night, the Punnamada lake and the Alappuzha beach make the quintessential Kerala postcard.
activities: Kettuvallam rice-barge on a palm-laced inland route.
Silent country boats through village waterways.
The snake-boat regatta on the second August Saturday.
The shore end of the backwater country.

destinations.name: Varkala
destinations.summary: Kerala's cliffs-and-coves beach town of sunset cafés.
destinations.description: A mineral-red cliff beach 55 km north of Thiruvananthapuram airport and 43 km from Varkala rail. The 40-ft cliff-top promenade, Papanasam beach and occupational funky cafés make it the state's bohemian favourite.
activities: Red-laterite path over the beach with whale-watching lookouts.
The sacred 'sin-washing' main beach beneath the cliff.
The cliff's sushi-and-smoothie sunset stool culture.
A 2,000-year-old Vaishnavite shrine by the beach.

destinations.name: Ooty
destinations.summary: The queen of the Nilgiris — botanic lawns around a lake.
destinations.description: Tamil Nadu's classic 2,240 m hill station, 88 km from Coimbatore airport and on the Nilgiri Mountain Railway. Botanical gardens, the Rose Garden, the tiny lake and Dodabetta above complete a Victorian original.
activities: Lawns, glass hothouses and a 150-year-old fossil tree.
A toyl-train run from Ooty through tunnels and tea fields.
Highest Nilgiri point (2,637 m) with telescope views.
A man-made lake ringed by eucalyptus at the town centre.

destinations.name: Kodaikanal
destinations.summary: The princess of hill stations — a star-shaped lake amid shola forests.
destinations.description: A 2,133 m plateau town 100 km from Madurai rail/air and 205 from Coimbatore. The boat lake, Coaker's Walk and the pillar-rock viewpoint reward a slow few days.
activities: Rowboats on a lake shaped by its basin's shoreline.
Sunset terrace with a telescope over the plains.
Sheer granite columns and a film-set forest gorge.
A forest-department trail to the plateau's blue lake.

destinations.name: Rameswaram
destinations.summary: The southern point where Ram built a causeway — temple sea rhythms.
destinations.description: An island at the eastern end of the Pamban bridge (rebuilt rail bridge 2023), 70 km southwest of Madurai airport, reached by a rail line over the sea. Ramanathaswamy temple and Dhanushkodi's ghost dunes anchor it.
activities: The longest corridor in Hindu temple architecture and 22 ritual tanks.
The cyclone-wrecked 1964 town stranded in white sand.
Drive or ride over the sea with the old train causeway beside.
Ritual dawn dip where the temple meets the sea.

destinations.name: Pondicherry
destinations.summary: The white-and-ochre French quarter of gated boulevards and Auroville.
destinations.description: A former French colony 150 km from Chennai airport on the TN coast, a 4-hour drive away. Promenade beach, the white quarter, Auroville's Matrimandir and heritage cafés give it a unique Gallic-South-Indian rhythm.
activities: Ochre villas, Hindu done-as-French styles and gated boulevards.
The meditative golden sphere of Sri Aurobindo's community, 12 km out.
Rocket park and sunrise jogging along the seawall.
Bakeries and bistros resurrected in the old quarter.

destinations.name: Delhi
destinations.summary: The layered capital of seven cities — monuments, megamalls and bazaars.
destinations.description: India's gateway, with Indira Gandhi airport, the metro and every rail connection. Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb and the Chandni Chowk anarchy collate 12 centuries in one sprawling canvas.
seasons: Check AQI; mornings can be heavy.
activities: A century-old citadel plus the spine of Old Delhi's markets.
The garden-tomb grammar that Georgians later copied for the Taj.
The 73 m victory tower and rust-resistant iron pillar.

destinations.name: Amritsar
destinations.summary: The Golden Temple's haloed sanctum and Sikh Punjab's heart.
destinations.description: Punjab's spiritual capital 25 km from the Wagah border and with rail/air from Delhi. The gilded Harmandir Sahib, Jallianwala Bagh and the border-beating ceremony make a moving 24-48 hours.
activities: The gold-domed gurdwara mirrored in the Amrit Sarovar tank.
The world's largest free kitchen serving 100,000 meals a day.
Twin-nation parade and flag ceremony at dusk, 28 km away.
The solemn 1919 massacre garden and memorial.

destinations.name: Chandigarh
destinations.summary: Le Corbusier's concrete garden city at the Himalayan doorstep.
destinations.description: A planned modernist capital at the base of the Shivaliks, where the expressways and cycle grids of Sukhna lake meet. Rock Garden, the Capitol complex and Punjab's bazaars make it a design-first stop.
activities: Nek Chand's reclaimed waste-city of mosaic figures and grottos.
Le Corbusier's Open Hand, High Court and Assembly buildings.
The dam lake with Shivalik silhouettes and boating.
Corbusier's shopping square and the city's food murmur.
